newsitem.title: NORWAY: Storebrand rejects Aker RGI doubts.
newsitem.headline: Storebrand rejects Aker RGI doubts.

text.p: Norway's Storebrand ASA on Wednesday dismissed doubts raised by industrial group Aker RGI ASA about redeeming preference shares in the insurance company.
Storebrand said the issuing of short-term preference shares formed a significant part of the refinancing of Storebrand in 1993 following a failed takeover bid in the insurance sector.
"The refinancing plan was approved by the Oslo Stock Exchange and the Norwegian Banking, Insurance and Securities Commission," a Storebrand statement said.
In an interview with Norwegian radio, Storebrand top executive Aage Korsvold said he was unhappy with Aker RGI's remarks, which came in an interview in financial daily Dagens Naeringsliv.
"I see it an unfriendly act to create uncertainty where there is no uncertainty," he said.
Aker RGI top executive Bjoern Rune Gjelsten was quoted by the Dagens Naeringsliv as questioning whether the rules for redeeming preference capital in Storebrand complied with securities legislation.
If Aker RGI's opinion prevails, it could torpedo the proposed merger between Storebrand and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse, the Dagens Naeringsliv said.
Aker RGI is a major shareholder in Storebrand, Norway's largest insurer.

The Storebrand statement criticised Aker RGI for saying it had obtained legal opinions "that support the idea that the holders of preference shares can in practice block a decision to redeem the preference shares".

"Storebrand is of the opinion that the purpose of the preference class of shares is clear, and the intention has been that it shall be possible to redeem the preference shares in 1998/99," the statement said.

"The company has adequate financial strength to implement such a redemption. Storebrand will therefore repudiate that there is any doubt about the redemption possibility, and strongly regrets the uncertainty that Aker RGI may have created."
